items.t: CVT can wear and lose speed (service campaign JSD)
items.job: CVT software update and inspection (campaign JSD)
items.note: Free at a Toyota dealer under the campaign. If code P2820 is stored, the campaign covers a new CVT; Toyota also set up a process for out-of-warranty cars.

items.t: CVT hesitation, slipping or sudden loss of power
items.note: Toyota's own time for a CVT swap on the iM is about 9 hours. A remanufactured unit costs less than a new dealer part. Check campaign JSD first.

items.t: High-pitched whine from the CVT once warmed up
items.job: Replace CVT valve body (bulletin S-SB-0001-19 / T-SB-0016-19)
items.note: Toyota bulletin T-SB-0016-19 lists valve body 35410-12871 and 3.1 hours (op code TC1804), plus pan and case gaskets, O-rings and about 6 L of CVT fluid. The parts range runs from a Toyota parts dealer's sale price to list price for the valve body; gaskets and fluid add a little more. The bulletin repair was covered by Toyota's 5-year/60,000-mile powertrain warranty, so ask a dealer about goodwill if you are just past it.

items.t: Check engine light with code P2820
items.note: If P2820 is already stored, the CVT campaign covers a new transmission at no charge.

items.t: Check engine light with code P2610
items.note: Toyota bulletin S-SB-0001-18 allows 0.4 hours to reprogram the engine computer; the high end allows for reading the code first. Toyota covered this under its 8-year/80,000-mile federal emissions warranty.

items.job: Install updated front brake pad kit

items.t: Water on the floor from a clogged A/C drain
Horn stops working (steering wheel spiral cable)
items.note: One owner was quoted about $900 at a dealer.

items.t: Pre-collision system warning or several warning lights at once
items.note: Covers diagnosis only. Recalibrating the camera or replacing a sensor costs more.
